basic_info.description: Back up offers are welcome. Whether you are a full time resident or looking for a pied a terre, this is a rare opportunity to live in a highly sought after cosmopolitan city by the bay.  Imagine living in the top floor corner unit of a registered historical building with panoramic views of the city and the bay. Located across from Buena Vista Park, with the Haight Ashbury District on one side of the hill and The Castro on the other. Originally built as a convent and hospital in the 1920's and converted to condominiums in the late 1980s. Designed by renowned architects Blackwell and Brown, who are known for designing the city of Paris Building, San Francisco City Hall, and the San Francisco Art Institute, just to name a few. Presented for the first time by the original owner, this home has been completely updated and refreshed. Residents can reserve the  onsite stain glass adorned chapel for their private parties. The location has quite a history and was featured in a scene from the noir film  "Vertigo"  by Alfred Hitchcock.
